handoff.purpose: Define mutation operators and the generate() function that produces a list of Mutants.

symbols.name: OPERATORS
symbols.note: Tuple of operator functions: DROP_CALL, INVERT_CONDITION, WEAKEN_COMPARISON, CHANGE_CONSTANT, DROP_ARGUMENT, EARLY_RETURN.

symbols.name: OPERATOR_CLASS
symbols.note: Dict mapping each operator to a defect class string.

symbols.name: generate
symbols.note: Generates count parseable mutants over real functions. Deterministic with given seed.

claims.text: Generate ``count`` parseable mutants over real functions. Deterministic.
claims.why: Function returns list of Mutants; uses random.Random(seed) and deterministic iteration.

claims.text: Collect candidate (file, function) sites once, then sample from them, so a big file cannot dominate merely by being walked first.
claims.why: Sites are collected in a list and then shuffled before sampling.

claims.text: Why each site was refused. Reported rather than discarded, because a filter nobody can see the effect of is the same shape of defect as a filter nobody calls -- see below.
claims.why: filtered dict is populated and later assigned to generate.last_filtered.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30: these filters were defined, documented as built, and CALLED FROM NOWHERE. Every one of SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS, _is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, _in_main_block and covered_lines appeared exactly once in this file -- its own definition.
claims.why: References symbols not in this chunk; cannot verify their definitions or usage.

claims.text: The corpus behind the published 75.3% detection figure was therefore minted without any of them, including on __repr__ bodies and log strings, which is precisely what they exist to exclude.
claims.why: References external corpus and detection figure; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Undetectable by construction. Keeping it would depress every score measured against this corpus for a reason that is not the detector's fault, which is exactly how a metric starts lying.
claims.why: trivially_equivalent check filters out such mutants and increments rejected count.

claims.text: Sites the no-go filters refused BEFORE a mutation was ever attempted. Published for the same reason as ``last_rejected``: a filter whose effect nobody can observe is one refactor away from being a filter nobody calls, which is exactly the state these were found in.
claims.why: generate.last_filtered is assigned with filtered items.

observations.what: Function generate sets attributes on itself (last_rejected, last_filtered) for inspection.
The comment about filters being defined but never called references symbols not present in this chunk.
CHANGE_CONSTANT appends '_x' for non-numeric constants, which may create invalid Python literals (e.g., True_x).
DROP_ARGUMENT always pops the last argument, regardless of function signature; may produce invalid calls.
